system.summary: Homophonic sign alphabet with up to three signs a letter, word signs (et, che, per, io, tu, voi, noi, quando, come, titles), nulls and numbers from 10 for names, per the key sheet MAP LXXII 183; six signs for doubled consonants and a sign for non are not on the sheet.
system.notes: The sheet gives the sign with the dotted dash for both n and c; Ridolfi writes d and l alike.

prior_solution.where: None found by the contributor for docs. 112, 113, 115 and 96; Desjardins (1859) prints the glossed doc. 114 only. Not re-searched by the project.

conditions.human_role: Contributed result (GitHub issue #589, Andrew Aymeloglu): AI agents matched the glossed word pairs of Ridolfi 107 and 110 to the key sheets of filza LXXII, transcribed the letters twice and read them; a second model reviewed; the contributor reviewed the result. The project checked and filed it.

solution.what: Andrew Aymeloglu (issue #589): the glossed word pairs of Ridolfi's letters MAP LXXIV 107 and 110 compared with the key sheets of filza LXXII; LXXII 183 reproduces them (44 of 44 letters on eight words, his figure; not held out).

The four letters transcribed twice from the 1272 px images by AI agents, the second pass blind and frozen before reconciling; alternatives recorded for every ambiguous sign (the contributor's record).

The sheet applied to Ridolfi 112, 113, 115 and Alamanni 96; six signs for doubled consonants and non added from glosses and from the words they make. Words graded strict, forced, lenient, doubtful, unread: Ridolfi 104, 90, 85, 2, 2 of 283; Alamanni 37, 24, 19, 0, 11 of 91.

The contributor's calibration: with the gloss of Ridolfi 107 c. 241v masked, the reader got 28 of 38 glossed words right (74%), 4 confidently wrong. His key-shuffle control: z = 18.5 (Ridolfi), 13.5 (Alamanni). Not repeated by the project.

Brice Dudout (comment on issue #589; his report, no files sent): the published key.json applied unchanged to the glossed Ridolfi letter MAP LXXIV doc. 114 (865 signs, his own frozen transcription) against Desjardins's printed text: character agreement 0.774 against 0.397 for the best of 200 shuffled keys; his bar was 0.85, so the test failed by his own rule; 101 of 175 words exact.

Integration check: aaymeloglu/own_decode.py, written from key.json and the transcriptions, gives the key output of reading.txt for all 283 and 91 cipher words and the contributor's tier counts. The key sheet (image 79536) and Ridolfi 112 c. 256r (image 81807) fetched from the ASF server: SHA-256 as in images.tsv; the sheet's alphabet is as key.json gives it; line 4 of c. 256r agrees with the transcription (about 45 signs). Other leaves not compared. Read share by the README rule set to the strict tier (36.7% and 40.7%).

The contributor's own held-out test on Ridolfi's glossed letter MAP LXXIV doc. 114 (issue #589, comment of 14 Nov, 21:44 UTC; aaymeloglu/held-out-114/). Declared beforehand: key.json at commit 46dec7b unchanged, a transcription of the gloss-masked cipher lines by an agent without gloss, values or print (865 signs), reference Desjardins I pp. 585-586, character agreement with any listed value of a two-valued sign counting, bar 0.85. Result 0.838 against 0.379 for the best of 1,000 shuffled keys: under the bar, failed. First value only 0.775. The promised count of exact words was not made. After the result, not pre-registered: 0.844 with two block ends corrected; 0.886 against the contributor's own gloss reading (partly cipher-assisted). Order of events and blinding by the contributor's record (one commit).

The contributor, from the gloss of doc. 114 (no longer held out) and the key sheet enlarged: the sign ÷ split into n (dot or tick above) and c (dot below only); Ridolfi's d and l separated by the arm at the baseline; a sign for ll (barred d-shape) added; bb glossed four times; the person sign with raised c glossed Re five times, the other read [il Duca] by inference from two glosses. The four letters relabelled from one-pass shape sorts (agents with the labels, not the values) and re-read: strict tier 193 of 283 (68.2%) and 51 of 91 (56.0%), from 36.7% and 40.7%. Gabbrielli no. 25 reported to be this alphabet (supports nn and rr), no. 34 a different one.

Check of the contributor's held-out test and revision (AI agent): SHA-256 of transcription-frozen.tsv, score.py and key-46dec7b.json as in PREREGISTRATION.md, the key equal to key.json at his commit 46dec7b; score.py read and re-run: 0.8382, 0.7745, shuffles best 0.3790 mean 0.2859; an own scorer written from the protocol gives 0.8382 and 0.7745 (0.8855 against his gloss reading; best of 300 own shuffles 0.362); own_decode.py on the revised files gives the key output of reading.txt for all 283 and 91 cipher words and the revised tier counts. Not checked: the reference against a copy of Desjardins, and the transcription of doc. 114, the shape sorts and the gloss reading against the images (the ASF server reset the connection on the evening of 14 Nov).

texts.label: Ridolfi to Piero de' Medici, Milan, 16, 21 and 30 October 1494

reading_review.by: project (maintainer session for Daniel Bourdeau, at the integration of issue #589), not the author of the reading
reading_review.note: Read the three letters end to end as Italian against the English, sentence by sentence: the cipher passages join the clear text into coherent sentences in all three (the King met by the Duchess Bona at Pavia castle; the Pavia citizens and the milling duty; the King's two hours at night with Bona and Isabella's refusal to appear; opinion in Milan that Florence cannot resist; Faenza promised to the Lady of Forlì), and the English follows the Italian clause for clause. Grade B, not A: 193 of 283 cipher words (68.2%) are free of a choice between sign values, 32 were chosen by sense, and the held-out test on doc. 114 came out at 0.838 under its 0.85 bar, so the connected text is a proposal. Weak passages: doc. 112 'lo edicto(?) ha fatto di fare ricomperare il dazio della macine' (rough syntax, no subject), 'non ne li strignerebbe(?)' and 'le poste siano legate in modo che ... da farne poco caso' (letters sound, sense proposed); the second person sign read [il Duca] by inference; doc. 113 'dice li quello intenderete [?] [?] da lui a bocca' (two groups unread, the clause does not close). Letters supplied in brackets (Pav[i]a, pr[efa]ta, M[aes]tà, a[p]resentarsi) are marked. The doubtful phrases of doc. 113 marked (?) outside the italics are in the clear hand, not the cipher. The sentence score of docs/_check_reading.py (31% clean) runs over the whole file, English and notes included, and is not a measure of the Italian.

texts.summary: Ridolfi reports from Milan as Charles VIII comes through Lombardy: the King received at Pavia castle by the Duchess Bona; the Pavia citizens' protest against the milling duty; on the day the death of Gian Galeazzo was announced, the King's night visit to Bona and Duchess Isabella's refusal to appear; opinion in Milan that Florence cannot resist the French. The key did not pass its pre-registered held-out test on doc. 114 (0.838 against a bar of 0.85), so the connected text is a proposal, not a validated reading.
texts.note: Reader's note (the project, 14 Nov 2026, revised the same evening), not a review grade: Read the Italian and the English of the three letters as sentences, and again the lines changed by the revision (alla camera, nel letto, della macine, non volle, cavallaro, nella città, alla corte, [il Duca]): they hold together and fit the dated events. 193 of 283 cipher words are now free of a choice between sign values, 32 were chosen by sense; the held-out test on doc. 114 came out at 0.838, under its 0.85 bar, so wrong words are to be expected. A connected proposal.

texts.label: Alamanni to Piero de' Medici, Vigevano, 26 April 1494
texts.summary: Alamanni privately urges Piero de' Medici that the King of Naples's plan to turn Genoa is the one remedy, must not be delayed and must be entered only with enough preparation, that name 22 will never trust the King, and that Piero must tell no one; on the last leaf, Lodovico's three threats, the second unread.
texts.note: Reading review, 2026-11-14 (project (maintainer session for Daniel Bourdeau, at the integration of issue #589), not the author of the reading): decoded, not read; no grade. Read as Italian against the English, sentence by sentence. Of about seventeen clauses that carry cipher words, about half hold (voltare Genova; farlo a tempo; a manifesta vittoria; sotto mantello; si fidi mai del re; volessi la guerra per mettere la città in travaglio; di serrarci la via) and the rest break: '[22] [?] [?] [?] et consigli buono in bocha'; 'tu qui(?) tu havessi(?) a schoprire', whose sense runs against the 'sotto mantello' that follows; 'vedessi di ferla(?) netta(?)'; 'vuol tanta grandeza(?) sua' between two gaps; 'con l'armata [?] Genova'; and on c. 221v the three threats, where the verb of the list and the second threat are unread ('da poter [?] [?] [?]', 'assai tenuto [?] ce la calerà(?) [?]'). The clear hand around the cipher has open gaps in most sentences of cc. 220r-221r, so the cipher clauses cannot be closed from their context. The English is not a translation of the whole: c. 220r and the end of c. 221v are summarised in brackets, sentences are cut with [...], and words are supplied that the Italian does not carry ('[I do not hold]', 'the sense wants something like harm us'). 51 of 91 cipher words (56.0%) are free of a choice between sign values; 9 are unread, 2 doubtful, 17 chosen by sense. To become a reading: a collated clear text, the nine unread words, and a full English. Earlier reader's note: Read the Italian and the English as sentences: the cipher passages fit the clear text around them, with 9 of 91 cipher words unread, 2 doubtful (ce la calerà) and 17 chosen by sense; 51 words are free of a choice between sign values. 'sotto mantello' now comes from the ll sign.
